critique.good: Example URLs stay fully intact (558px ≥ 537px word), so no mid-word splits anywhere; Option is intact at 152px; the Default format string wraps cleanly into two token-preserving lines; Description at 240px is comfortable and never exceeds two lines.
critique.problems: It overflows the 720px box by 431px. Horizontal scrolling means that when the reader scrolls right to read Example/Description, the Option anchor scrolls out of view, which destroys the row-by-row lookup this table exists for. Default (200) and Description (240) are also wider than their content needs, inflating the scroll for no benefit.
critique.cause: Example 558 + Option 152 already consumes 710px, leaving ~9px for two more columns; the 1151px total comes from insisting on intact URLs while also being generous to Default and Description.

critique.good: Fits the 720px box with no scroll; Option intact; row heights are the most even of the three (36/60/83/106/106/83); Description is legible.
critique.problems: Example URLs break mid-word (e.g. 'db.int/ernal') because 250px is far below the 290px two-line threshold; log.pattern still runs to four lines; some Description cells are 4–5 lines. Proportions are backwards: Default (165px) is far wider than its 90px longest token needs, while Example — the widest content — is starved.
critique.cause: Example 250px (text 229px) cannot hold the 537px URL; Description 152px (text 131px) is too narrow for 501px prose; Default 165px is wasted width that cannot reduce its line count until ~200px.

critique.good: Fits the box; Example 300px crosses the ~290px threshold so long URLs wrap to two lines with fewer splits than r0B; Option intact.
critique.problems: Description at 127px is severely starved, ballooning cells to six lines and rows to 153px; the table grows to 591px tall and the prose column dominates the rhythm. One mid-word split remains in Example, and Default 140px is tight.
critique.cause: Allocating 300px to Example consumes the budget, leaving Description only 127px (text 106px) for 501px of prose, which forces ~5–6 lines.

critique.good: Option is exactly wide enough for auth.jwksUri and cache.ttlSeconds, so the row anchor stays intact; all four columns are visible; Description has enough width for 2-3 line prose.
critique.problems: Default is still too narrow for log.pattern, which breaks into four lines. Example at 230px (209px content) is far below the 537px URL width, producing three mid-word splits and making the postgres/auth URLs hard to copy and compare. Row heights inflate to 83-106px.
critique.cause: The 197px Description allocation takes width away from Default and Example. Default at 140px is below the roughly 161px needed to reduce log.pattern to three lines, and Example at 230px forces the long URLs to break arbitrarily.

critique.good: Best no-scroll compromise: Option intact at 152px; Default 111px is exactly the token-safe minimum (90px content); Example 290px is just enough (269px content) to hold the 537px URL on two lines; Description 166px keeps prose at 2-4 lines; only one split remains.
critique.problems: Default is at its bare minimum and log.pattern still needs four lines. The remaining URL split is visually ugly, and Description is narrow enough that the longest prose runs to four lines. There is no spare width to improve either without crossing a line threshold.
critique.cause: The widths [152,111,290,166] sit on three thresholds at once: Option needs 131px content, Default needs 90px for its longest token, and Example needs just over 268px to keep the 537px URL on two lines. Moving width from Example to Description pushes the URL to three lines; moving it the other way adds a Description line. This is why r1B is already the optimal 720px squeeze.

critique.good: No mid-word splits: Option and Default tokens stay intact, Example URLs are fully readable on one line, Description is comfortable at 200px, and the table is shorter at 428px.
critique.problems: The table is 1076px wide and overflows the 720px box by 356px. Description is entirely off-screen at the initial scroll, so the reader loses the meaning column while scanning, and horizontal scrolling breaks row-by-row comparison. Default at 165px is wasted because log.pattern still wraps to four lines.
critique.cause: Example is given its full 558px while Default and Description are also over-allocated: 165px Default does not reduce its line count, and 200px Description adds width without shortening the table further. The no-split goal is valid, but the allocation is inefficient.

critique.good: Option and Default identifiers stay intact, the Example URLs remain on one line, and there are no mid-word splits. The three visible columns are clearly separated.
critique.problems: At 720px the table overflows by 302px, so Description is completely off-canvas and the row loses its meaning while the reader is looking at it. Example is over-wide and mostly empty on short rows, while Default is too narrow: log.pattern breaks into four short lines, making that row visually heavy. The table reads as a three-column table, not the intended four-column one.
critique.cause: Example=558 is sized to the 537px URL token; Default=111 leaves only 90px of text, so the format string wraps at nearly every token. The 1022px total forces horizontal scrolling and hides Description.

critique.good: Option, Default, and Example stay intact; reducing Description to 166px trims some overflow and makes the table slightly more compact.
critique.problems: It still overflows by 268px, so Description remains offscreen. The change only shortens an invisible column, so it does not fix the reading problem. Example still dominates, and log.pattern still wraps to four lines in the narrow Default column. The table still reads as three columns with a large empty Example field on most rows.
critique.cause: Example=558 plus the minimum Option/Default widths already exceed 720px; shaving 34px from Description cannot bring the total under the box. Default=111 remains far below the 334px one-line default string, so the format string stacks.

understanding.purpose: A configuration reference table: readers scan option names, compare defaults with concrete examples, and consult descriptions for meaning.
understanding.reading: Row-by-row lookup, with Option as the anchor; Default and Example are compared as parallel values, while Description is supporting prose read only when needed.
groups: Option + Description: name and meaning for each row
Default + Example: parallel value columns with the same comparison role
keep_intact: Example URLs and log-format strings where possible
may_wrap: Default values at spaces between tokens
Example URLs only when accepting word splitting in a no-scroll design

bad.why: Example is compressed to 230px, causing three mid-word splits in URLs/identifiers (e.g. 'wel'/'l-known' and 'production_'/'main'), which is damaging in a code-reference table.
The table is 1076px wide and overflows the 720px box by 356px, forcing horizontal scrolling and clipping Description.
Overflows by 302px; the wide Example column pushes Description out of view, so readers cannot compare value and meaning without scrolling.
Overflows by 268px and hides Description; it pays the cost of horizontal scrolling without eliminating all wrapping in other columns.

final.rationale: This is a configuration reference, so identifiers and literal values need to stay scannable and copyable; the Example column carries the only truly long tokens and should receive the dominant share of width. r1B fits the 720px box, gives Example 290px, and limits damage to one benign hyphen break while keeping rows compact. The overflow designs buy fewer splits by forcing horizontal scrolling and hiding Description, which is worse for row-by-row comparison. r3B is a credible fallback, but it spends width on Default and starves Description, making the table taller.

general: Set a column's floor from its longest unbreakable token plus padding; code/URL columns should not go below that unless horizontal scrolling is acceptable.
Give the column with long machine-readable values the dominant width; short scalar columns can be narrow.
For a compact reference table, prefer one benign break over horizontal scrolling, but avoid multiple mid-token breaks in identifiers and URLs.
Narrowing Description raises every row's height; total width fitting is not enough if the table becomes a tall ribbon.
specific: Option needs about 152px because 'cache.ttlSeconds' is 131px; it cannot shrink without splitting.
Example needs roughly 290px to keep the PostgreSQL and JWKS URLs at two lines; 230px produces three ugly splits.
Default can be 111px because most values are short; only the log pattern wraps to four lines.
Description at 166px wraps to four lines; at 132px it dominates row height and makes the table 567px tall.

final.tradeoffs: A designer could accept horizontal scrolling to keep every token unbroken (r1C/r2A/r2B), or accept a taller table with a narrower Description (r3A/r3B). The chosen compromise prioritizes no horizontal scroll and compact rows over eliminating every break.
final.uncertain: Whether a single hyphen break in 'well-known' is acceptable in a code table; whether r3C's smaller height is worth its extra mid-word split; and whether r3B's 544px height is preferable to r1B's tighter 474px.

A.why: All columns fit in view, option names stay intact, and descriptions remain readable. The connection string and URL split across several lines.

B.why: The wider example column reduces token wrapping, but descriptions become narrow and ragged, making rows taller and harder to scan.

C.why: The example and description columns strike a useful balance: long examples take two lines and most descriptions remain readable. The logging pattern still wraps heavily.

D.why: Examples fit reasonably well, but the narrow description column produces many short lines and tall rows, while the extra default width has limited benefit.

E.why: Near-equal columns leave examples too narrow: the connection string and URL split repeatedly within tokens, making them difficult to read.

F.why: The long example stays on one line, but the description column lies beyond the initial viewport and requires horizontal scrolling; large row heights also leave substantial empty space.

reviews.unsure: A is a close alternative: it gives descriptions more room but breaks the long examples into more fragments. The tradeoff depends on how often readers need to inspect those tokens.

A.why: Everything fits in the viewport, and the examples have room, but the narrow description column creates many short lines. The database URL also splits within its hostname.

B.why: The wide example column keeps tokens largely intact, but the description is entirely offscreen and the example extends beyond the viewport. The tall rows leave substantial empty space.

C.why: The description is easy to scan and all columns fit onscreen. The narrower example column wraps the URLs across several lines, including a split within the JWKS path.

D.why: Examples have useful space and the table fits onscreen, but the narrow description column produces short lines and a particularly tall cache row. The database hostname also breaks across lines.

E.why: The nearly equal columns give excess space to short defaults while squeezing the long examples. Both URLs split repeatedly, making them difficult to follow.

F.why: The examples and descriptions have a workable balance, and all columns fit onscreen. The URLs wrap, including a break in the database hostname, but the descriptions remain reasonably readable.

reviews.unsure: C is a close alternative: it favors readable descriptions, while F gives the long examples more room. The preferred balance depends on how often readers need to inspect or copy the URLs.

A.why: Sensible pecking order: Option keeps its 131px identifier intact, Default is trimmed to what it needs, and the leftover space goes to Description, which reads in 2–3 clean lines. Rows stay compact and comparable. The cost is the Example column (~190px), where the postgres URL and JWKS URL break into 3 lines, though at tolerable points (after dots/slashes) rather than mid-word fragments.

B.why: Example is given ~300px while Description is squeezed to roughly 110px, so prose collapses into 4–5 short lines and the table becomes very tall and ragged on the right. The URL still breaks inside a word ("internal.e / xample.com"), so the width spent on Example buys little.

C.why: Example at ~300px gets the URLs down to two lines and Description is a bit wider than B, so the right side is less shredded. But Description is still narrow enough to run 3–4 lines, and the URL break leaves a line starting with ".example.com:5432/production_main", which reads awkwardly and is easy to misread when copying.

D.why: Space is wasted on Default (~150px for content whose longest token is 90px) while Description is crushed to ~110px and runs to five lines per row. The table reads as a stack of tall, unevenly filled cells; the column that needs width most is the one that got least.

E.why: Default is widened again and Example drops to ~190px, so the postgres URL shatters into five fragments ("postgr / es://app:secr / et@db.internal.exam …"). Breaking a copyable connection string mid-token like that defeats the purpose of the Example column, even though Description reads acceptably.

F.why: Example is given its full ~537px one-line width and Description is pushed entirely outside the 720px frame, so a reader sees Option/Default/Example and must scroll horizontally to read any description at all. For a config reference where the description explains the option, hiding it is the worst possible trade.

reviewsOld.unsure: Column widths were estimated from the rendered images rather than exact pixel values, so B/C and A/C margins are close; also unclear whether the host page allows horizontal scrolling (which would soften F) or whether mid-token URL breaks could be avoided by a word-break setting, since that is fixed content.

A.why: All four columns fit, but Description is squeezed to ~130px, so every sentence breaks into 4–5 short lines and rows grow tall; Example is also too narrow for the long token and splits it mid-word ("internal.e / xample.com").

B.why: The table overflows the 720px frame: Description is pushed entirely off-screen, forcing horizontal scrolling to read half the content, while Example holds a huge empty area and rows are ~100px tall of whitespace. Column proportions are wildly unbalanced.

C.why: The four columns are close to proportional to their roles: Option and Default compact, Example and Description each ~200px. All columns are visible without scrolling, long URLs break at punctuation (".", "/") rather than inside words, and descriptions settle at 2–4 lines, giving even row heights and a calm scan.

D.why: Example gets comfortable width and breaks the URL cleanly at ".example.com", but Description is the narrowest column at ~150px, so the cache row sprawls to six lines and rows become tall and uneven relative to the compact Option/Default columns.

E.why: Example is starved of width while Description is over-fed: the postgres URL fragments mid-token into "secr / et@db.internal.exam / ple.com:5432/produc / tion_main", damaging identifiers that readers need to copy exactly, and the left columns sit next to large blank areas.

F.why: Gives Example the room it needs — the URL breaks cleanly after "internal" and ".example.com" — while Description stays readable at 2–4 lines and Option/Default remain compact. Slightly less balanced than C because Description is narrow enough to hyphenate prose into short rags.

reviewsOld.unsure: I am estimating pixel boundaries by eye, so the exact Description/Example split in C vs F may be closer than it appears; I also assume B's off-screen Description is not intended as a deliberate scroll design.
